extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and computational algebra users (Magma users) working with finitely-presented groups and character computations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reference for constructing and computing with finitely-presented groups, manipulating words and relations, transferring groups between categories (polycyclic, permutation), computing quotients (abelian, p-quotient), and using coset enumeration/Todd–Coxeter in Magma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schur indicator applicability and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Schur indicator is +1 if a character x is orthogonal and −1 if x is symplectic. These functions only apply to powers χ^n with 2 ≤ n ≤ 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘This is not a real restriction since the technique is almost never useful for larger values of n.’ Example: Schur(x^6,2) returns −1 indicating symplectic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component functions for tensor powers (Orthogonal/Symmetric/Symplectic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions OrthogonalComponent(x,p), SymmetricComponent(x,p), SymplecticComponent(x,p) return the respective component of x^n corresponding to a partition p of n (2 ≤ n ≤ 6); OrthogonalComponents(x,n), Symmetrizations(x,n), SymplecticComponents(x,n) return the list of such components for n (2 ≤ n ≤ 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results may be generalized characters. Example: SymplecticComponents(x,2) produced two components whose Norms were 1, showing a splitting of x^2 into two irreducible characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition(T,y) usage for removing known irreducibles
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition(T,y) takes a sequence T of m characters (usually irreducibles) and a character y and attempts to express y as y = q1*T[1] + ... + qm*T[m] + z, returning Q = [q1,...,qm] of cyclotomic field elements and residue z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If T contains all irreducibles in y then Q gives coordinates of y in basis T; otherwise z is the residual character after removing those in T. Use to strip known irreducibles from a newly produced character y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferring fp-groups to polycyclic category (pQuotient / PCGroup)
rubrics_metrics.description: pQuotient(G,p,c) returns the class-c p-quotient P of an fp-group G and the natural homomorphism φ: G → P; PCGroup(G) returns a polycyclic group H isomorphic to G (and an isomorphism φ) when G is a finite soluble permutation or matrix group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If G is a finite p-group with class less than c, pQuotient will return a polycyclic group isomorphic to G. Use these transfers to leverage efficient polycyclic-group structural tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferring to permutation group category (CosetAction / CosetImage)
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetAction(G,H) returns the homomorphism φ: G → T defined by action on right cosets of H, T itself, and where possible the kernel of φ; CosetImage(G,H) returns just the image group T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If H is core-free (contains no nontrivial normal subgroup of G), φ will be faithful — enabling a faithful permutation representation. Use CosetImage when the homomorphism is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality threshold for trivial-subgroup CosetAction
rubrics_metrics.description: Using CosetAction with H the trivial subgroup yields a faithful permutation action but is practical only if |G| is moderate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual suggests practical use only if G has order at most about 100,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: FreeGroup construction and generator naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct FreeGroup(n) to obtain the free group of rank n; the generators are accessible as G.i and may be renamed via generator assignment, e.g., F3<a,b,c> := FreeGroup(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renaming generators gives shorter/meaningful printnames and can be used wherever F3.i would be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forming words and coercion via integer sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Words can be formed by multiplying generators/inverses or by coercing an integer sequence into the free group (positive i is generator i, negative −i is its inverse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eltseq(w) returns the integer sequence for w and #w returns the length. Example: F3![1,-2,-1,-1,-1,2,2] produces a*b^-1*a^-3*b^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word ordering and comparison rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of a free group are ordered first by length, then lexicographically. Generators are ordered: first generator, its inverse, second generator, its inverse, etc. Relational operators compare free reductions of words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided show how gt/lt behave based on length and lexicographic ordering; note that if group has relations, comparisons use free reductions only (not implied equalities by relations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations representation and accessors
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation w1 = w2 is represented using '=' (not ':='). For relation r, r[1] or LHS(r) returns left side and r[2] or RHS(r) returns right side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating relations on the generators does not change the group's definition until used in a quotient; relations may be mutated using sequence operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: quo-constructor semantics for fp-groups
rubrics_metrics.description: The quo-constructor quo< group | elements > forms the quotient of group by the normal closure of the elements; for fp-groups the right-hand side is regarded as a relations-clause defining the relation normal subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements in the relations-clause may be simple relations, relation lists (several words equated), words (converted to w=1), sets/sequences of words or relations, or subgroups (whose generators are taken as relators). The identity may be given as '1'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-constructor vs quo-constructor
rubrics_metrics.description: Group< generators | relations > constructs an fp-group in one step (free group and quotient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group-constructor is only available for quotients of free groups. For quotients of other fp-groups, use quo< >.

rubrics_metrics.name: FPGroup(G) for obtaining presentations of concrete groups
rubrics_metrics.description: FPGroup(G) constructs a presentation for a finite permutation or matrix group G on its defining generators and returns an fp-group isomorphic to G (and surjection φ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practical cutoff depends on resources but ~1,000,000 is typical. Use parameter StrongGenerators := true to get a presentation on an expanded (strong) generating set for larger groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access functions for finitely-presented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions like Generators(G), Ngens(G), Relations(G), and GeneratingWords(G,H) provide access to defining generators, their number, defining relations, and generators for subgroups as words in the generators of G (if known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to inspect and manipulate presentations and subgroup generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: AbelianQuotient and AbelianQuotientInvariants usage
rubrics_metrics.description: AbelianQuotient(G) constructs the derived quotient G/G' and returns it (as GrpAb) together with the natural surjection φ: G → A; AbelianQuotientInvariants(G) returns the invariant factors and torsion-free rank as a sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the sequence as [d1,...,dr, 0,...,0] with di | di+1; zeros count the torsion-free (infinite cyclic) factors. Use this to detect infiniteness and structure (examples: Z/2 + Z/6 + Z).

rubrics_metrics.name: pQuotient algorithm outputs and parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: pQuotient(G,p,c) returns the largest p-quotient P of G having lower exponent-p class at most min(c,63) as a polycyclic group (GrpPC), and the natural surjection φ: G → P. Parameters: Print (0–3) controls diagnostic output; Exponent may enforce xm = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print = 0 (no output) to 3 (more detailed). Exponent := m enforces exponent-law xm=1 on G before quotienting. A process version exists for fine-grained control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine relevant primes for pQuotient from abelian quotient
rubrics_metrics.description: The primes for which G may have nontrivial p-quotients can often be deduced from the structure of the abelian quotient of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if AbelianQuotient(G) ≅ Z/2 + Z/38 then relevant primes include 2 and 19 (19 divides 38).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower p-central series definition (for p-quotients)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lower p-central series Φ1(G)=G, Φ_{i+1}(G) = [G, Φ_i(G)] Φ_i(G)^p for i ≥ 1 is used by the p-quotient algorithm to construct successive quotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The p-quotient algorithm constructs quotients with respect to successive terms of this series and reports progress and class achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Todd–Coxeter procedure: nature and interpretation of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Todd–Coxeter is a procedure (not guaranteed to terminate) that attempts to construct the action of G on right cosets of a subgroup H and produces a coset table and index if successful. Functions invoking it include ToddCoxeter, Index, CosetSpace, CosetAction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the enumeration fails to complete within resources these functions return 0 — this indicates failure to complete, not a mathematical conclusion (e.g., cannot assume infinite index). Try different parameters or more sophisticated methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Todd–Coxeter parameter CosetLimit
rubrics_metrics.description: CosetLimit gives an upper bound on the number of cosets that may be defined at any stage of enumeration; default ≈ one million divided by number of generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard enumerations often introduce many more cosets than the final index; increase CosetLimit when necessary for large-index enumerations (example: enumerations failed at 1000/2000 but succeeded at 3000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Todd–Coxeter parameters Print and Grain (verbosity controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Print controls the level of informative printing during enumeration (0 none, 1 final statistics, 2 periodic messages). Grain sets frequency (every Grain cosets) for periodic messages (default 10,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print = 2 plus a small Grain helps observe trends (RD alive, Max, Total) that indicate whether enumeration is likely to complete. Example output shows RD alive, Max, Total and final Index, Max, Total.

rubrics_metrics.name: Todd–Coxeter parameter Hard (strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard is a boolean indicating expected difficulty; Hard = true processes relators in coset-table style rather than relator style (Hard = false is default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Switching Hard can dramatically change resource usage and success for difficult enumerations. Example: with Hard := true different Max/Total values observed and enumeration succeeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: sub-constructor and ncl-constructor for subgroups in fp-groups
rubrics_metrics.description: sub< G | ... > defines a subgroup H either by generators (words) or by specifying the action/homomorphism φ: G → Sym(n). ncl< G | ... > defines a subgroup by normal generators whose normal closure gives the subgroup (requires Magma to construct the normal closure, so finite index is necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgroups defined this way will often be presented only by coset tables and lack explicit defining relations. To convert such a subgroup into an fp-group with relations, explicitly apply a rewriting algorithm (see Section 30.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of undecidability of word problem for fp-groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Word problem for finitely-presented groups is in general undecidable (Novikov–Boone); normal forms are usually unavailable, so algorithms differ from those for concrete group representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine detailed structural information about a finite fp-group, explicitly construct an isomorphic group in a category with structure normal forms (permutation, matrix, or polycyclic categories) and apply the corresponding specialized tools.
